findings.title: Use OR for team admin/owner authorization
findings.body: The team permission check requires the caller to be both a team admin and a team owner. These are alternative membership roles, so a team admin or owner who is not also the booking organizer or an attendee is rejected with FORBIDDEN. Combine the checks with OR so either authorized role can add guests.

findings.title: Update the calendar using the booking organizer's credentials
findings.body: The handler allows attendees and team administrators to add guests, but constructs EventManager with the caller and the caller's credentials. The booking's calendar references belong to the organizer, not necessarily the caller. When an attendee adds guests, the organizer's calendar event therefore cannot be reliably updated, even though the new attendees have already been persisted. Load the booking owner's credentials and use that owner for the calendar update.

findings.title: Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist
findings.body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased, but incoming guest addresses are compared without normalization. An address such as Blocked@example.com passes validation and bypasses a blacklist entry of blocked@example.com, allowing invitations to addresses explicitly configured as blocked. Normalize incoming addresses before performing this comparison.

findings.title: Deduplicate guests on the server before inserting attendees
findings.body: The variable uniqueGuests only filters addresses already in the booking; it does not remove duplicates within the request. The server schema accepts duplicate addresses, so a direct request containing the same new email twice sends both entries to createMany, resulting in duplicate attendee records or an insertion failure if uniqueness is enforced. The dialog's client-side refinement does not protect the API; enforce uniqueness on the server.

findings.title: Honor event-type email suppression when sending guest updates
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally sends organizer and attendee emails and accepts no event-type metadata. Other booking notification paths honor disableStandardEmails.all.host and disableStandardEmails.all.attendee. Adding guests consequently sends standard notifications even for event types explicitly configured to suppress them, potentially duplicating custom workflow notifications. Pass the event-type metadata through and apply the same suppression checks.
